articles.title: India's first AI -piloted fighter jet programme unveiled. What makes FWD Supreme a ...
articles.content: India's first AI-piloted fighter jet programme, FWD Supreme, aims to bring a new dimension to aerial warfare by combining autonomous flight, long-range combat capabilities and coordinated operations involving multiple unmanned fighter aircraft. Developed by Bengaluru-based Flying Wedge Defence & Aerospace (FWDA), the programme seeks to change the way air combat is conducted by deploying AI-powered fighter jets that can share information, make coordinated decisions in real time and operate together as a formidable combat force. The company unveiled a full-scale static prototype of FWD Supreme on Tuesday, marking a major step in its ambition to develop a family of affordable, AI-piloted fighter aircraft. The FWD Supreme Heavy is being developed as an AI-powered autonomous fighter jet in the 1,500 kg-plus class, capable of carrying a payload of approximately 350 kg. According to the company, it is designed to incorporate a 5 kN propulsion system and achieve a maximum speed of Mach 0.8 to Mach 0.85. Its cruising speed is expected to be around 500–600 km/h. The aircraft is expected to have a range exceeding 1,500 km, an endurance of more than two hours, and will feature a flying-wing configuration and an internal weapons bay. Its approximate dimensions are 10 metres by 10 metres. Together, these proposed capabilities are intended to give FWD Supreme the speed, reach, payload capacity and autonomy required for combat operations, the company stated. The programme's defining feature is FWDA's Mobbing Doctrine, an approach that seeks to use multiple AI-piloted fighter jets as a coordinated combat force. Instead of relying on a limited number of expensive, high-value aircraft, the doctrine envisages deploying several autonomous fighters that operate together, much like a swarm of jets. These aircraft would share information and make coordinated decisions in real time, allowing them to function as a networked force rather than independent platforms. The objective is to create an operational advantage through numbers, autonomy and coordination. Another important aspect is the ability to absorb losses without compromising the overall mission. By deploying capable autonomous aircraft at scale, the programme seeks to change the economics of air combat. This approach could allow a coordinated group of AI-piloted aircraft to continue operating even if some platforms are lost during a mission. The programme is being developed in phases, beginning with a smaller variant called FWD Supreme Lite. Designed for the Army, the Lite variant is a 250 kg-class demonstrator that also serves as a test bed for the larger programme. According to FWDA, the aircraft has already completed taxi trials and is being prepared for its first flight in the next two months. The company says the Lite variant is already 90 per cent indigenous and is equipped with an Indian-made engine manufactured by UMS in Coimbatore. FWDA also plans to integrate a Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) engine into the programme to further reduce dependence on foreign components. “We are looking to integrate the DRDO engine to make it completely indigenous, reducing any delay and dependency on foreign components,” said FWDA's Suhas...

PNN Published At: 14 October 2026 4:12 pm Published on: 14 October 2026 4:12 pm SUBSCRIBE Fredna Dental Systems Expands Advanced 3D Imaging Expertise Into Veterinary Healthcare With India’s First Dedicated Veterinary CBCT Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], October 14: Fredna Dental Systems (FDS), India’s largest dental diagnostic centre , has expanded its expertise in advanced three-dimensional imaging into veterinary healthcare with the introduction of India’s first dedicated CBCT (Cone Beam Computed Tomography) machine for veterinary applications through Fredna Vet Diagnostics (FVD) . FDS’ specialised veterinary division, DentXVet , supports the interpretation and reporting of CBCT examinations. Unlike conventional two-dimensional radiography, CBCT produces detailed three-dimensional images that allow anatomical structures to be evaluated from multiple planes. articles.title: Hyundai Bayon India Launch on October 26, 2026
articles.content: Hyundai Motor India has unveiled the India-spec Hyundai Bayon, with the SUV scheduled to launch on October 26, 2026. Positioned as an Intelligent Utility Vehicle, the Bayon focuses on artificial intelligence, connected technology and an immersive digital cockpit. It will be powered by a 1.5-litre petrol engine producing 115hp and 144Nm, paired with either a six-speed manual transmission or an Intelligent Variable Transmission (IVT). Bookings are now open across authorised Hyundai dealerships and on the company's official website for ₹11,000. The Hyundai Bayon will be powered by a four-cylinder, 1.5-litre MPi petrol engine producing 115hp and 144Nm of torque. Buyers will have the option of a six-speed manual transmission or Hyundai's Intelligent Variable Transmission (IVT). The combination of a naturally aspirated petrol engine and two transmission options gives customers a choice based on their driving preferences. Hyundai has not disclosed the Bayon's fuel-efficiency figures in the supplied announcement. The Hyundai Bayon features a digital cockpit built around two 12.3-inch curved panoramic displays. The screens bring together driving information, navigation, entertainment and connected functions, creating an integrated interface for the driver. The cabin also features Hyundai's Connected Car Navigation Cockpit (ccNC), accelerated by NVIDIA. The system incorporates advanced graphics, online onboard navigation, split-screen functionality, a personalised control panel and smartphone-like quick controls. Hyundai has also incorporated individual user profiles and a multilingual interface supporting 10 regional and two international languages. These features are designed to make the vehicle's digital functions more accessible to customers across India. Technology is the primary highlight of the Hyundai Bayon, with the SUV introducing Hyundai Motor India's first-ever Generative AI Voice Assistant alongside connected services and over-the-air software updates. The Bayon introduces Hyundai Motor India's first Generative AI Voice Assistant, featuring Intelligence by Perplexity and Voice AI powered by SoundHound AI. Unlike conventional voice recognition systems that rely mainly on predefined commands, the assistant is designed to understand conversational requests and provide relevant responses. Drivers can ask it to prepare travel itineraries, provide real-time weather information, suggest hotels and restaurants, recommend nearby shopping destinations, and share sports updates and information. The system is intended to make interactions between the driver and vehicle more natural while helping occupants access useful information during their journeys. The Connected Car Navigation Cockpit (ccNC) combines connected services, navigation and vehicle controls in a unified digital interface. Accelerated by NVIDIA, it offers advanced graphics, online onboard navigation, split-screen functionality and quick-access controls. The interface is designed to make frequently used functions easier to access while providing an integrated experience across the dual 12.3-inch displays. The Hyundai Bayon supports Controller Over-the-Air (C-OTA) updates for up to 19 vehicle controllers. These updates enable supported software enhancements to be delivered remotely, without requiring a dealership visit for every update. According to Hyundai, this technology will allow compatible features and software to evolve over time while helping reduce maintenance requirements associated with software updates. The SUV will come equipped with Hyundai Bluelink, offering more than 70 connected features. These include remote start and stop, connected vehicle...

articles.title: Enlight Metals Launches India's First Agentic AI -Enabled Marketplace for Metals
articles.content: Enlight Metals Private Limited, India’s first Agentic AI-enabled metal procurement platform, today announced the launch of its marketplace for metals, designed to transform how businesses discover suppliers, evaluate sourcing options and connect with potential buyers. By bringing buyers and suppliers onto a common platform, the marketplace aims to make metal procurement more transparent, accessible and efficient. Moving beyond conventional, relationship-driven sourcing, the marketplace enables buyers to explore multiple suppliers, compare available options and assess supplier credibility before making procurement decisions. At the same time, suppliers gain greater visibility among buyers actively seeking the products they offer. Supplier profiles, platform onboarding checks and buyer reviews can help users make more informed decisions, while access to multiple sourcing options can support competitive pricing, quality assurance and more dependable transactions. The marketplace covers six primary product categories: flat steel, structural steel, TMT bars, value-added steel products, pipes and tubes, and ferro alloys. Its portfolio includes over 25 steel products and grades, including hot-rolled and cold-rolled steel, galvanized coils and sheets, structural beams, angles and channels, mild steel pipes, cable trays, slotted angles and earthing strips, among other industrial steel products. Designed to address the fragmented nature of traditional steel procurement, the platform serves manufacturers, original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), infrastructure companies, EPC contractors, fabricators and renewable energy businesses. It aims to help buyers identify suitable suppliers, evaluate sourcing options, compare commercial terms and coordinate fulfilment with greater efficiency. Enlight Metals is developing an AI-enabled procurement ecosystem that brings together product specifications, supplier matching, pricing, availability and delivery requirements. Its roadmap includes capabilities such as demand forecasting, procurement planning, inventory optimisation and automated replenishment, with the objective of helping businesses anticipate material requirements and make more informed sourcing decisions. Dhananjay Goel, Managing Director, Enlight Metals Private Limited, said, “Metal procurement has traditionally been a fragmented process, where discovering the right supplier, comparing prices, assessing quality and verifying credibility can require considerable time and effort. Our marketplace is designed to change this by bringing buyers and suppliers closer together through a more transparent and technology-led ecosystem. Buyers can explore multiple options and assess supplier credibility, while suppliers can connect with a wider pool of relevant customers. We believe this can improve sourcing efficiency, encourage more competitive deals and help both sides make better-informed decisions.” The marketplace launch builds on Enlight Metals’ broader vision of transforming metal procurement through technology and operational expertise. Following its recent USD 1.5 million funding from Exar North Group Inc. at a USD 10 million valuation, the company plans to strengthen its technology infrastructure, expand its supplier network and broaden product availability. It also intends to enhance logistics coordination and fulfilment capabilities to support growing customer requirements. As India’s industrial ecosystem expands, Enlight Metals aims to make steel sourcing more organised, responsive and accessible. The company will continue to expand its product portfolio in line with customer demand and its ability to ensure reliable sourcing and fulfilment.

articles.title: Fredna Dental Systems Expands Advanced 3D Imaging Expertise into Veterinary ... - The Blunt Times
articles.content: Building on its expertise in advanced dental and maxillofacial imaging, Fredna Dental Systems extends specialised CBCT capabilities to veterinary diagnostics through Fredna Vet Diagnostics and DentXVet. Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], October 14: Fredna Dental Systems (FDS), India’s largest dental diagnostic centre , has expanded its expertise in advanced three-dimensional imaging into veterinary healthcare with the introduction of India’s first dedicated CBCT (Cone Beam Computed Tomography) machine for veterinary applications through Fredna Vet Diagnostics (FVD) . FDS’ specialised veterinary division, DentXVet , supports the interpretation and reporting of CBCT examinations. The introduction of this machine marks an extension of Fredna Dental Systems’ capabilities in high-resolution CBCT imaging, radiographic interpretation and specialised reporting into the veterinary space, bringing advanced imaging infrastructure and expertise to the diagnostic evaluation of companion animals. Unlike conventional two-dimensional radiography, CBCT produces detailed three-dimensional images that allow anatomical structures to be evaluated from multiple planes. In veterinary diagnostics, this can enable more precise assessment of dental, maxillofacial, cranial, nasal and other complex osseous structures , particularly in cases where detailed anatomical visualisation is important for diagnosis and treatment planning. The technology can provide greater clarity on the location, extent and orientation of abnormalities, and can be particularly valuable in evaluating trauma, fractures, dental pathology and other conditions involving complex hard-tissue structures . Commenting on the introduction, Mr. Fredun Medhora, Director, Fredna Dental Systems , stated, “At Fredna Dental Systems, our focus has always been on advancing the role of specialised imaging and diagnostics in enabling more precise clinical decision-making. Extending this expertise into veterinary healthcare through India’s first dedicated veterinary CBCT is a natural progression of that vision. Through Fredna Vet Diagnostics, we are bringing this capability into a specialised veterinary environment, supported by the infrastructure and expertise required to make advanced imaging more accessible to veterinarians. For us, this is about taking our experience in advanced imaging beyond conventional boundaries and contributing to the evolution of specialised diagnostics in animal healthcare.” Speaking about the diagnostic relevance of the technology, Dr. Vinayak Umesh Shirsekar, Director, Fredna Dental Systems , stated, “CBCT records detailed hard-tissue information of the maxillofacial region, including the teeth and bone. This makes it particularly valuable in evaluating trauma, facial and cranial fractures, as well as dental fractures. It can help determine the number, location, direction and extent of a fracture, whether fractured segments are displaced, and whether vital structures are involved. In dental cases, it can also help assess the extent of a crack or fracture within a tooth and its relationship with surrounding structures. These findings can be valuable for risk assessment and treatment planning.” The imaging capability at FVD is supported by DentXVet , the specialised veterinary division of Fredna Dental Systems, which provides radiographic interpretation and reporting for CBCT examinations conducted at Fredna Vet Diagnostics. With the introduction of dedicated veterinary CBCT, Fredna Dental Systems is extending its imaging and reporting expertise beyond human dental diagnostics into veterinary healthcare, bringing together advanced technology, specialised interpretation and veterinary-focused diagnostics through FVD and DentXVet....

articles.title: World Students' Day 2026: Date, Significance and APJ Abdul Kalam's Legacy
articles.content: World Students’ Day 2026 will be marked on October 15, the date which will celebrate the birth anniversary of former Indian President and renowned scientist Dr APJ Abdul Kalam. The occasion marks the importance of education, innovation, scientific thinking, and youth empowerment, thus showcasing Kalam’s lifelong commitment to inspiring students and nurturing young talent. Although famously known as World Students’ Day, the observance is not officially acknowledged by the United Nations (UN). October 15 is designated by the UN as the International Day of Rural Women. World Students’ Day 2026: Date and Theme World Students’ Day will be celebrated on Thursday, October 15, 2026. There is no formally announced theme for this year. The day focuses on boosting access to quality education, stirring creativity, promoting scientific curiosity, and empowering students to contribute to society. Schools, colleges and other educational institutions mark the occasion through seminars, debates, science exhibitions, cultural programmes and interactive sessions. These activities encourage students to develop leadership skills, explore new ideas and understand their role in national development. Who Was Dr APJ Abdul Kalam? Avul Pakir Jainulabdeen Abdul Kalam was born on October 15, 1931, in Rameswaram, Tamil Nadu. He rose from a modest background to become one of India’s most respected scientists and the country’s 11th President, serving from 2002 to 2007. Kalam studied physics at St Joseph’s College in Tiruchirappalli before finishing aerospace engineering at the Madras Institute of Technology. He began his scientific career at the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and later joined the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO). He played a crucial and momentous role in developing India’s first Satellite Launch Vehicle, SLV-III, which successfully sent the Rohini satellite into near-Earth orbit in July 1980. His contributions to the country’s missile development programme fetched him the title ‘Missile Man of India’. Kalam also contributed to the Pokhran-II nuclear tests in 1998. In recognition of his tremendous contributions to science and defence technology, he was awarded the Bharat Ratna, India’s highest civilian award, in 1997. Despite his scientific achievements and presidential responsibilities, Kalam maintained a close bond with students. He believed education was essential for national progress and motivated youth to dream ambitiously, think independently, and achieve their goals. After completing his presidential term, he moved to teaching and continued interacting with students. He died on July 27, 2015, while delivering a lecture at the Indian Institute of Management Shillong. Why Is World Students’ Day Significant? The observance emphasises on making education accessible, inclusive and relevant to changing economic and technological needs. It also draws attention to challenges such as unequal educational opportunities, the digital divide, student stress and gaps in vocational training. Moreover, Kalam’s vision emphasised that education should also include integrity, discipline, creativity and social responsibility. articles.title: Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Birth Anniversary: The legacy of his dreams - Organiser
articles.content: It is the darkness before dawn. In the lanes of Rameswaram, a boy runs from door to door with a bundle of newspapers. His father ferries people in a boat to feed the family. There are few comforts at home, but values in abundance. Who could have told this boy that the headlines he was delivering would one day carry his own name, and that he would rise to the highest constitutional office in the land? It is said that circumstances may decide where a person begins, but never where he ends up. Kalam’s life is living proof of this truth. He did not accept hardship as his destiny; he turned it into fuel. Curiosity, a hunger to learn and discipline carried him to a height at which his name is written in letters of gold in the history of Indian science. When India forged its own wings After Independence, India faced a great challenge: technological self-reliance. The economy was still laying its foundations, and ahead lay the steep climb of space and defence science, a summit India urgently needed to scale. At ISRO, Dr Kalam played a key role in developing SLV-3, India’s first indigenous satellite launch vehicle. In 1980, this same vehicle placed the Rohini satellite in Earth orbit. It was the dawn of national self-confidence, for India had realised that it could carve out an identity of its own in space. Then, at the DRDO, with the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme, he gave a new direction to the nation’s strategic capability. His association with projects such as Prithvi and Agni earned him the title “Missile Man of India”. In an era of dependence on foreign technology, every experiment in his laboratory was an act of national self-respect. Under his leadership, an entire generation of scientists gained the conviction that Indian talent could solve the most complex challenges. Even at the Summit of Power, Dr Kalam Remained a Student In 2002, Kalam became India’s 11th President. The grandeur of Rashtrapati Bhavan did not touch his nature. He took the office beyond the walls of formality and turned it into a forum for dialogue with students and young people. He asked questions, listened to the answers and taught every child to believe in their own potential. His words carried little of the burden of preaching and much of the warmth of lived experience. Even at the peak of scientific achievement, he called himself a lifelong student. When did greatness ever mean, for him, becoming bigger than others? His definition was to put one’s abilities to work for the betterment of society. A dream that will not let you sleep For Dr APJ Abdul Kalam, a dream was never a picture drifting through sleep. A dream was the idea that never allows you to sit at ease, and that pushes you towards your goal every morning. It was this thinking that made Wings of Fire an inspiration to millions of readers.
